messages.author: a8d8d5c676a7609b
messages.subject: power of a matrix
parts:
Hi,

Can I raise a square matrix to a power? Not elementwise, but where the result of Q^n is is Q matrix-multiplied by itself n-1 times. I understand that pow() doesn't do this. I could use eigenvectors * eigenvalues^n * eigenvectors^-1, but eigenvalues_sym and eigenvectors_sym require a symmetric matrix and Q is not symmetric.

Thanks for any help,
Paul

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: power of a matrix
parts:
On Thursday, October 2, 2014 7:00:02 PM UTC-4, pcdjo...@gmail.com wrote:
Can I raise a square matrix to a power? Not elementwise, but where the result of Q^n is is Q matrix-multiplied by itself n-1 times. I understand that pow() doesn't do this. I could use eigenvectors * eigenvalues^n * eigenvectors^-1, but eigenvalues_sym and eigenvectors_sym require a symmetric matrix and Q is not symmetric.

No, but you can just loop it
for(i in 1:(n-1)) Q <- Q * Q;

 Ben

I hadn't thought of this before because it isn't possible in JAGS -- still learning the differences. My main motivation for changing from JAGS to Stan was that Stan appears to allow more matrix operations.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] power of a matrix
parts:
JAGS could do this with an array to store intermediate
values:

Q[1] <- original_Q %*% original_Q;
for (n in 2:N)
Q[n] <- original_Q %*% Q[n-1];

Then you'd get your result in Q[N] = original_Q^N.
And a whole lot of intermediate outputs you would not want
to monitor.

We spend a fair bit of time suggesting that people don't
literally translate JAGS code like the above to Stan but
to use reassignment.

We could certainly add a matrix power operator. I added
a feature request, but did not assign it to anyone or make
it an immediate priority:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/1073

I would suggest putting the loop in a function for the time
being.

functions {
matrix matrix_pow(matrix a, int n) {
if (n == 0)
return diag_matrix(rep_vector(0, rows(a)));
else if (n == 1)
return a;
else
return a * matrix_pow(a, n - 1);
}
}


- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] power of a matrix
parts:
I wasn't aware that I could use an array to do this in JAGS (I'm almost as new to JAGS as I am to Stan). Here is the JAGS code that worked, with the help of a local user (QW is the original 4x4 matrix, QWt[t, 1:4, 1:4]  is QW^t):

          QWt[1, 1:4, 1:4] <- QW
          for (gen in 2:t) { QWt[gen, 1:4, 1:4] <- QW %*% QWt[gen - 1, 1:4, 1:4] }

Many thanks for your help,
Paul
